papers.title: Thermoplastic polyurethane as a base material for soft, high-density neural interfaces
papers.abstract: Polymers used as substrate and encapsulation for implantable devices are typically deposited layer-by-layer, leaving polymer-polymer interfaces that adhere poorly and become a critical failure point. Thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) elastomers combine four properties not found together in any other candidate: decades of clinical use in long-term implants and availability in medical grade, a stiffness well below that of polyimide and parylene C, compatibility with microfabrication, and thermoplastic self-fusion, which removes the polymer-polymer interface entirely. This work introduces TPU as a base material for soft, high-density neural interfaces and demonstrates one route to realizing them. Gold is patterned on a sacrificial copper sheet by maskless lithography and transferred into TPU by vacuum lamination, giving conformally coated tracks down to 15 um at 30 um pitch within a single, merged polymer body. An additional electroplating step produces a nanostructured pinecone gold surface that increases the electrochemically active area of the electrodes, approximately doubling the charge injection capacity. Daisy-chain silicon chips were also embedded within the soft polymer body. The films transmit up to 88% at 470 nm, a wavelength commonly used for optogenetics. TPU showed no cytotoxicity towards differentiated SH-SY5Y cells and only a mild tissue response after 9.5 months of subcutaneous implantation in rats.

papers.title: A Novel Computational Framework to Investigate the Biomechanics of Burrowing
papers.abstract: Head-first burrowing likely imposes strong mechanical demands on the skull of fossorial vertebrates, but how cranial tissues respond to these loads remains obscure. Here, we developed a computational framework integrating the discrete element method (DEM) with finite element analysis (FEA) to investigate cranial biomechanics during burrowing. We used Blanus cinereus, a round-headed amphisbaenian, as a model to establish DEM predictions that were validated and calibrated against in vitro experiments across three substrates and compared with in vivo push forces. DEM-calibrated particle contact forces were then transferred to an anatomically detailed finite element model to quantify cranial loading. The analyses suggested that soft tissues accommodated substantial deformation, while the skull transmitted burrowing loads from the premaxilla towards the occipital region. Cranial sutures further redistributed stresses and strains within the skull. This validated DEM-FEA framework links particle-scale substrate interactions with internal cranial biomechanics and provides a quantitative approach for investigating the mechanics of head-first burrowing across fossorial vertebrates.

papers.title: Chronic Electrophysiology Captures Progressive Variability in DNA-Damaged Cardiac Networks
papers.abstract: Electrophysiological recordings provide a key functional readout of cardiac health. Most in vitro studies rely on acute measurements rather than recording evolving functional changes. Here, we implement a microelectrode array (MEA) based system for chronic electrophysiological monitoring of human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocyte (iPSC-CM) monolayers. Electrophysiology recordings were maintained for up to 40 days, enabling longitudinal assessment of field potential amplitude, field potential duration, beat frequency, conduction velocity, and waveform morphology. Untreated iPSC-CM monolayers exhibited stable electrophysiological behavior throughout chronic culture. Following exposure to the cardiotoxic chemotherapeutic doxorubicin, chronic recordings captured progressive deterioration in electrical activity, including reduced field potential amplitude, altered repolarization dynamics, increased beat-to-beat variability, and reduced conduction that persisted after drug removal. Electrode-resolved analyses further revealed pronounced progressive spatial variability, highlighting localized responses that would be obscured by population-averaged measurements. Endpoint assays indicated reduced calcium transient amplitude and altered calcium reuptake, decreased mitochondrial membrane potential, and loss of connexin 43, findings consistent with the impaired electrical activity observed in chronic recordings. Together, these results establish chronic electrophysiological monitoring as a powerful approach for resolving the spatiotemporal progression of cardiotoxicity and other dynamic cardiac processes in vitro.

papers.title: Matrix-modulated Air-liquid Interface Microenvironments Reveal Architectural Control of Lung Tumor Phenotypes
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma evolves within a highly structured microenvironment shaped by air exposure, basement-membrane ligands and three-dimensional (3D) organization, yet standard in vitro models capture only fragments of this architecture. Here, we systematically disentangle how air-liquid interface (ALI), extracellular matrix (ECM) cues and dimensionality interact to regulate tumor epithelial states. Using five architectural configurations, we demonstrate that these parameters act synergistically to promote distinct morphological, transcriptional and inflammatory phenotypes not observed under conventional 2D or submerged 3D cultures. ALI broadly enhanced epithelial cohesion, progenitor activation, partial EMT programs and cytokine expression, whereas ECM embedding further induced ALI-mediated mesenchymal activation, matrix remodeling and invasive cytoskeletal organization. Notably, 3D ALI uniquely produced a hybrid alveolar-mucinous phenotype characterized by concurrent SP-C and MUC5B induction, alongside integrated epithelial, basal and mucosecretory identities. These emergent states reflect tumor-relevant plasticity and illuminate architectural controls over lineage infidelity, invasion and inflammatory activation. Together, these findings establish ALI-ECM-dimensionality intersections as critical regulators of lung tumor phenotype and provides a systematic architectural framework for designing more physiologically relevant in vitro lung cancer models.

papers.title: Pocket-Conditioned Generation and Down-Selection of Non-Oxime Reactivators
papers.abstract: Acetylcholinesterase reactivation is a structure-constrained design problem in which chemical plausibility, access to central nervous system, pocket compatibility, and reactivation geometry must be considered together. We report a computational workflow for generating and down-selecting candidate non-oxime reactivators in the paraoxon-inhibited human acetylcholinesterase pocket. For generating the candidates, the first-round utilitezed pocket-conditioned DrugFlow, but due to solubility issues, the second-round candidates were output form FlexFlow, DrugFlow-OOD, DrugFlow preference alignment, and pocket-specified BoltzMol-1. A property-guided DrugDiff output provided a protein-unconditioned baseline. Although 93.9% of the DrugDiff subset passed Lipinski criteria for druglikeness, its median synthetic accessibility (SA) score signalled that it was difficult to synthesize compared against other generative approaches. A strict predicted blood-brain barrier and solubility gate retained 31.0% of Base DrugFlow, 61.0% of FlexFlow, 27.5% of DrugFlow-OOD, 3.8% of DrugFlow-PA, and 35.1% of BoltzMol-1. The second-round top-ten lists had lower SA scores and higher quantitative estimate of drug-likeness (QED) values than the DrugDiff shortlist, while DrugDiff had fewer aggregate heuristic violations. This work compares the best performing generative drug discovery models with suggested down sleection approaches for human acetylcholinesterase reactivation.

papers.title: Nose-to-Knee Transplantation for Osteochondral Regeneration: A Proof-of-Concept Study in Sheep Employing Ceramic-Hydrogel Osteochondral Grafts
papers.abstract: Osteochondral defects remain a major clinical challenge, frequently progressing to osteoarthritis and ultimately requiring joint replacement. Despite advances in regenerative strategies, current approaches often fail to restore the structural and functional complexity of the osteochondral unit, resulting in poor integration and limited long-term performance. Here, we developed autologous osteochondral grafts combining mechanically mature nasal chondrocyte-derived cartilage with a 3D-printed strontium-hardystonite-gahnite trabecular bone scaffold, which was tested in an osteochondral defect model in sheep. Nasal chondrocytes were encapsulated in a hyaluronan transglutaminase-alginate hydrogel generating hyaline-like cartilage with physiologically relevant compressive properties (1.0 +/- 0.2 MPa) after 6 weeks of in vitro maturation. MicroCT scans of the osteochondral unit were used to design biomimetic trabecular bone scaffolds. Controlled infiltration of the hydrogel into the trabecular pores and subsequent cartilage maturation created a mechanical interlock between cartilage and bone layer, reaching an interfacial shear strength of 201 +/- 42 kPa. The translational potential of this approach was evaluated in a proof-of-concept ovine study. The engineered cartilage remained attached to the bone scaffold for three months following implantation, but osteochondral repair was limited by implant sinking, likely caused by inadequate implant fixation in the defect, resulting in micromotion, synovial fluid infiltration, osteolysis and subsequent bone cyst formation. Together, this work demonstrates the feasibility of engineering mechanically mature autologous osteochondral grafts while identifying subchondral bone integration as the primary bottleneck limiting successful osteochondral regeneration and future clinical translation.

papers.title: Surfactant-Enhanced Hybridization Capture for Direct Sequence-Specific RNA Extraction from Plasma and Whole Blood
papers.abstract: Direct recovery of low-abundance RNA from complex biological samples remains a major challenge for ultrasensitive detection. Sequence-specific hybridization capture enables selective enrichment, but recovery from crude samples is compromised by RNA degradation, protein interference, RNA secondary structure, and target sequence variation. Here, we address these limitations with a sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS)-based formulation that not only lyses virions and protects RNA, but also directly accelerates hybridization kinetics, substantially reducing the need for thermal denaturation. This enabled direct RNA capture from crude plasma or whole blood with near-quantitative recovery, outperforming a widely used silica-based kit at low input. Without centrifugation or plasma separation, we detected HIV RNA by RT-qPCR at 25 copies/mL directly from whole blood. We further developed a free energy ({Delta}G)-guided algorithm for mutation-robust probe design, achieving >85% mean recovery across HIV-1 subtypes with a single probe. This work opens low-abundance RNA biomarkers in crude biofluids to ultrasensitive detection, addressing a major barrier to early diagnosis.

papers.title: FLEX-DBS: a flexible wireless platform for bilateral constant-current deep brain stimulation in freely moving rodents
papers.abstract: Background: Preclinical deep brain stimulation (DBS) in rodents is central to understanding how DBS works, but most rodent DBS is delivered through a tether, which constrains behavior, home-cage experiments and uninterrupted stimulation. Most long-runtime wireless mouse stimulators achieve their runtimes by setting stimulation parameters before or around implantation and operating from supplies of about 3 V. New method: FLEX-DBS (Flexible Deep Brain Stimulation) is a head-mounted, battery-powered stimulator that delivers bilateral constant-current stimulation from improved Howland current pumps on +/-5 V rails. Amplitude, pulse width and frequency are programmable in continuous and burst modes from an iOS application over Bluetooth Low Energy, and stimulation continues autonomously after the phone disconnects. The device measures 19.5 x 22.5 x 8.72 mm, weighs 3.71 g in operation and runs on two size-13 zinc-air cells, which are exchanged by briefly detaching the device, pausing stimulation only for the exchange. Results: Into a 1 k{Omega} bench load, delivered current increased approximately linearly with the amplitude setting and was repeatable from pulse to pulse, with an asymmetric biphasic waveform whose recovery phase ran at about one fifth of the stimulating amplitude. Battery current was 1.47-1.89 mA in standby and 3.15-3.42 mA during stimulation at amplitude settings of 60-400 A, giving a projected three days of continuous stimulation per pair of cells. Firmware v0.5 left a net charge of 26-35 % of the stimulating-phase charge per pulse into 1 k{Omega}. Into 47 k{Omega}, within the in vivo load range, stimulating current was compliance-limited at 93 A. Pulse-derived estimates of the effective load presented by five implanted platinum electrodes in three mice had weekly means of 43-54 k{Omega} over eight weeks (32-80 k{Omega} across individual sessions), placing the maximum regulated current near 90 A (81-101 A at the weekly means). Analysis of the current-pump network bounds load-dependent current error at 3-8% for these loads. In vivo, we delivered cingulate FLEX-DBS at high amplitude settings intended to evoke a robust stimulation-associated behavioral phenotype in six mice. Time spent immobile in an open field rose from 46.5% at baseline to 75.7% during stimulation (a 62.7% increase in the group mean) and remained elevated after stimulation ended; without a sham control, this increase cannot be separated from within-session habituation. Comparison with existing methods: Among the published wireless rodent stimulators compared here, several offer some of these capabilities, but none combines bilateral constant current output, real-time wireless control that continues as autonomous stimulation after disconnect, and both continuous and burst modes; FLEX-DBS does so at the cost of runtime measured in days rather than weeks. Conclusions: FLEX-DBS is designed for untethered DBS experiments in which parameters must be set, changed and verified at the cage. Its measured power consumption permits a projected three days of continuous operation per cell pair; firmware v0.5 requires improved charge balancing before prolonged in vivo stimulation. The electrode load, rather than the programmable range, sets the usable stimulation amplitude in vivo. In vivo, stimulation at high amplitude settings was associated with increased immobility, consistent with effective stimulation through implanted electrodes; electrode impedance and delivered current were not measured in these mice.

papers.title: Antiviral Sulfonated Polymersomes Inhibit Corona-, Influenza-, and Alphavirus
papers.abstract: A broad-spectrum antiviral is required to enable rapid intervention against current, newly emerging and mutating viruses. Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), influenza A virus (IAV), Sindbis virus (SINV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) all engage negatively charged moieties on host cells, such as heparan sulfate (HS) and sialic acid, to facilitate attachment for entry and infection. We designed HS-mimetic nanoparticles in the form of polymer vesicles (polymersomes) by blending membrane-forming and sulfonated copolymers. These biocompatible polymersomes successfully inhibited host cell infection of HS-dependent SARS-CoV-2 and HS-independent IAV in vitro with sub-nanomolar potency. Multivalent interaction of several virus ligands with a single polymersome as quantified by fluorescence correlation spectroscopy likely contributes to their potency. The sulfonated polymersomes also functioned in vivo as demonstrated by a reduction in the spread of SINV, an alphavirus model for CHIKV, in zebrafish embryos, which led to a significantly increased survival. Hence, our polymersomes could form the basis for an urgently required multifunctional broad-spectrum antiviral nanomedicine.

papers.title: Rational Design of 5' UTRs for Optimized mRNA Expression and Cost-Effective, Rapid Analysis of Capped mRNA
papers.abstract: In vitro-transcribed (IVT) messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics require rigorous quality control of 5' capping efficiency and 3' poly(A) tail length, both of which constitute critical quality attributes (CQAs). Current analytical workflows for these CQAs rely on hybridization with nucleic acid probes and biotin-based affinity purification, which constrain throughput and increase per-assay cost. Here, we report a rationally designed 5' untranslated region (5' UTR) that sustains high translational efficiency while enabling probe-free, one-step purification for rapid quantification of capping efficiency and poly(A) tail length distribution. This approach exploits a strategically engineered 5' UTR incorporating a purine-only RNase A-resistant fragment terminating at a single pyrimidine cleavage site, together with a translation-enhancing element comprising an N6-methyladenosine (m6A) deposition motif and an 18S rRNA complementarity sequence. This dual-function design accommodates GA-rich sequence segments without compromising mRNA translational output. Compared with conventional probe- and biotin-dependent workflows, the present method substantially reduces cost and processing time and is compatible with simultaneous detection of segmented AmGn poly(A) tail variants. This integrated platform provides a simplified, probe-free and construct-universal for high-throughput in-process control (IPC) of mRNA therapeutics.

papers.title: Design and characterization of peptide-responsive biosensors
papers.abstract: Gram-positive bacteria use secreted peptides and peptide-responsive transcription factors for quorum sensing. Here, we demonstrate that intracellular expression of these peptide effectors with their cognate transcription factors leads to regulation of gene expression in both in vitro and in vivo systems. Because both effector and regulatory parts can be readily expressed, complex circuits, including auto-activation schemes, can be developed, with switch-like behaviors. Moreover, the peptide effectors can be fused to proteins, enabling a direct intracellular readout of translation and potentially allowing any protein to encode regulatory interactions in cells. Our results support a foundation for regulatory circuits that extend beyond canonical components such as LacI and TetR.

papers.title: Quantitative 3D imaging of intact engineered heart tissues using inverted selective plane illumination microscopy
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Advanced in vitro models of the human heart have become promising tools for studying cardiac diseases and drug discovery. Three-dimensional (3D) engineered heart tissues (EHTs) provide more adult cardiac tissue-like structural organization compared to traditional two-dimensional (2D) in vitro models with straightforward contractile readouts. However, the assessment of the architecture of EHTs, especially the quantification of cellular and tissue structural components, has remained poorly studied. Here we demonstrate the use of light-sheet microscopy for structural imaging of intact EHTs and provide quantification of the EHT cellular and subcellular structures. Methods We developed an in-house inverted selective plane illumination microscopy (iSPIM) platform and combined it with iterative indirect immunofluorescence (IT-IF) staining for better signal acquisition. We developed an image-processing and analysis pipeline dedicated to volumetric EHT analysis. Results With this integrated platform, we achieved volumetric imaging of intact EHTs and quantification of 3D tissue architecture, revealing aligned cardiomyocytes within the imaged volume and increasing cardiac nuclei content towards the core of the tissue. The developed methods allowed the detection of heterogeneities between tissue sections, demonstrating the sensitivity required for future disease modeling or maturation studies. Conclusions The developed integrated platform opens new possibilities for volumetric analysis and characterization of 3D tissue structure using iSPIM, providing new insights into EHT architecture and the use of EHTs as disease modeling tools.

papers.title: Large-Scale Mutagenesis Identifies Sequence Changes That Bias Tau Toward CTE-like Aggregation
papers.abstract: Tau amyloid fibrils adopt disease-specific structures across tauopathies, yet the sequence determinants that favor one pathological fold over another remain poorly defined. Here we combine computational saturation mutagenesis and energetic profiling, in vitro aggregation, cryo-EM and cellular seeding assays to identify sequence changes that alter tau fold compatibility. Across six tauopathy fibril structures, approximately 12,000 substitutions revealed that mutational sensitivity is concentrated within interaction networks formed by amyloidogenic motifs rather than uniformly distributed across the fibril core. Comparison of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) folds identified residues within the 335-363 region that differentially influence fold compatibility. The S341L/S352I double mutant accelerated aggregation and remodeled packing within the PAM4-containing amyloidogenic region, producing an alternative amyloid architecture in a minimal tau fragment. S341L/S352I biosensors preferentially responded to CTE-derived over Alzheimer's disease-derived seeds, while aggregates generated from recombinant S341L/S352I tau exhibited CTE-like cellular templating behavior. Although these assemblies are not established to reproduce the atomic CTE fold, the results demonstrate that targeted sequence changes can bias tau aggregation and propagation toward a CTE-compatible state. This framework provides a strategy for defining sequence-structure relationships in polymorphic amyloids and developing conformation-selective models and biosensors.

papers.title: Rapid simulation of organ-scale oxygen transport for tissue ischemia prediction
papers.abstract: A densely vascularized tissue can still be starved of oxygen. Tissue oxygenation depends heavily on vessel arrangement, blood flow distributions, and cellular metabolism. Resolving these effects from individual constituent vessels to whole organs has historically been computationally prohibitive. We introduce the Cardiovascular Analysis and Simulation of Circulatory Advection, Diffusion, and Exchange (CASCADE) toolkit, which makes vessel-resolved oxygen transport tractable at the organ scale through a novel screened Green's-function formulation. On laptop-class hardware, CASCADE simulates networks containing thousands of vessels in under one second and a full biventricular human heart model in about two minutes. We validate spatial oxygen and cell-survival predictions against experiments in perfused engineered tissues and matched finite-element simulations. In engineered tissues, sweeps across thousands of network designs and physiological conditions reveal when vessel density, oxygen supply, or network architecture limits viability, establishing design rules for sustaining thick constructs. In a human heart model, CASCADE translates coronary occlusion, anemia, polycythemia, and hypoxemia into distinct myocardial oxygenation patterns, revealing where oxygen delivery fails and how much tissue is at risk.

papers.title: A minimally modified AAV9 variant (AAV9fyhr) for enhanced CNS gene delivery by intra-CSF administration.
papers.abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) mediated gene therapies continue to show promise for the treatment of genetic diseases. However, delivery and safety still represent significant prohibitive barriers restricting translation of these delivery modalities to humans. We describe a novel AAV9 variant, AAV9fyhr or FYHR, identified from screening a controlled randomization point mutation AAV9 library in mice and nonhuman primates followed by directed evolution of in vivo CNS-derived libraries screened in human iPSC differentiated cortical neurons. Capsid variants of interest were identified by coupling long read sequencing and computational structure modeling. Structure-function analysis of our lead candidate reveal that two targeted amino acid changes are sufficient to result in beneficial pleiotropic effects across viral stability, cell surface attachment, and gene delivery. We developed a novel multiplexed barcoding reporter system, enabling a time and cost-effective option to gather spatially resolved single cell capsid validation data in mice and nonhuman primates. When administered intrathecally, AAV9fyhr exhibits 2-to-6-fold higher gene delivery across several tissues in the CNS while minimally altering the tropism to peripheral tissues in comparison to AAV9. These findings demonstrate the potential of whole capsid engineering for the rational development of translational next generation AAV capsids.

papers.title: MINT: Predicting Enzyme-Cofactor Specificity by Multimodal Knowledge Transfer from Protein-Ligand Interactions
papers.abstract: Protein-cofactor selectivity prediction is important for enzyme annotation, metabolic engineering, and biocatalyst discovery, but it remains challenging because experimentally supported associations are limited and unevenly distributed, and because biologically relevant differences can be subtler than those captured by general protein-ligand interaction models. Here, we present MINT (Multimodal Interaction Network with Teacher supervision), a multimodal framework for cofactor specificity prediction. MINT combines protein sequence features with cofactor sequence and graph representations and is trained with a gradual adaptation strategy that transfers useful information from a pretrained protein-ligand interaction model to the cofactor prediction task. On a fixed balanced held-out test set, MINT achieved the best overall performance among all compared methods (AUC = 0.932), and this ranking was reproduced in an independent family-stratified evaluation at the natural positive rate (pooled AUC = 0.939). Further analyses suggest that the pretrained model provides transferable structural information, while the gradual training scheme helps adapt that information to cofactor specificity. In a case study of the chemically near-identical NAD/NADP pair, MINT recovered 95.0-98.6% of true binders and resolved a single-phosphate-level distinction with direct relevance to engineering enzyme cofactor specificity. These results show that gradual transfer learning is an effective approach to cofactor specificity prediction when annotation is limited.

papers.title: Evaluation of Densified Collagen Tubes as an Interposition Graft in Abdominal Aorta
papers.abstract: A major challenge in vascular tissue engineering is the development of scalable fabrication methods capable of producing vascular grafts with suitable mechanical properties and hemocompatibility for both preclinical evaluation and future clinical translation. Using a recently developed method to generate acellular vascular grafts from densified collagen hydrogel, we present a proof-of-concept in vivo evaluation of the scalable collagen graft technology. Thick-walled, genipin-crosslinked grafts, representative of a fabrication approach applicable to clinically relevant vessel sizes, were implanted as interposition grafts in the rat abdominal aorta. These grafts supported rapid neointima formation and re-endothelialisation of the luminal surface but developed late thrombosis, highlighting the challenges of evaluating clinically scalable grafts in small-animal models. To enable assessment of the platform in millimetre-scale vessels, we developed a thin-walled (~100 {micro}m), non-crosslinked graft using a constrained densification approach and hyaluronic acid-mediated modulation of collagen fibril assembly to improve compliance matching and hemocompatibility, with the latter providing a matrix-level approach that may complement surface-bound antithrombotic coatings. These grafts remained patent for up to 17 weeks and exhibited neointima formation, re-endothelialisation, and early cellular infiltration into the graft wall. Together, these findings demonstrate in vivo functionality of densified collagen vascular grafts and establish a foundation for future evaluation in larger animal models.

papers.title: Biohybrid toggle switches: leveraging bistability in muscle-actuated machines
papers.abstract: Tissue-engineered skeletal muscle offers robotics unique advantages in energy density, adaptability, and self-repair, but current biohybrid machines couple muscle directly to artificial skeletons, limiting net force output and requiring continuous stimulation maintain mechanism positions. Here, we introduce a biohybrid bistable switching mechanism that converts antagonistic muscle contractions to snap-through actuation of an elastomeric four-bar flexure, maintaining stable positions without energy consumption. We decouple passive muscle pre-tensioning from flexure operation with thin-film elastomer resistance bands, enabling fine tuning of spring stiffness and force to match muscle mechanical output envelopes. Leveraging mesoscale additive manufacturing, spin coating, and replica molding techniques, components are integrated into a millimeter-scale linear stage to axially align muscles with artificial components. Our prototype achieves reversible toggling between bistable states with a 130 ms switching time, establishing skeletal muscle actuators as viable electromechanical switches, and broadening biohybrid robotics towards novel applications such as grippers, valves, and mechanical computers.

papers.title: Unsupervised 3D classification and characterisation of osteocyte and chondrocyte lacunae in the murine osteochondral unit
papers.abstract: In the murine osteochondral unit, morphology of chondrocyte lacunae (CCL) within calcified articular cartilage and osteocyte lacunae (OCL) within the underlying subchondral bone reflects local biomechanical conditions that are altered in disease, making reliable discrimination of both lacunar populations important for studying osteochondral physiology and pathology. Histology is generally considered the gold standard for identifying CCL and OCL. However, it is inherently limited to two-dimensional assessment and a relatively small tissue section, restricting comprehensive characterisation of three-dimensional lacunar structure. Synchrotron-radiation micro-computed tomography (SR-microCT) enables volumetric quantification of lacunae; where classification is typically based on the position of each lacuna relative to the cement line separating calcified cartilage from bone, requiring manual delineation of this convoluted interface. Such approaches are labour-intensive, operator-dependent, and rely on access to specialised synchrotron infrastructure that is not widely available. To address these limitations, we present a fully automated, annotation-free pipeline for classifying OCL and CCL in the mouse osteochondral unit based on desktop micro-computed tomography (microCT), independent of cement line identification. The proposed unsupervised workflow requires neither tissue separation nor labelled training data, enabling objective and scalable discrimination of lacunar populations directly from volumetric image data. Seven morphometric and positional features per lacuna were extracted from SR-microCT and desktop microCT datasets and analysed using Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP). Validation of the pipeline outcome on SR-microCT against manual classification across specimens yielded very-high agreement, with Gwet's AC1, the Matthews correlation coefficient, and balanced accuracy each approaching 0.99, in both healthy and post-traumatic osteoarthritis specimens. Such a workflow can be readily adapted for the investigation of osteochondral interface in various other species.

papers.title: Benchmarking longitudinal local centiles for radiographic knee osteoarthritis prognosis
papers.abstract: Cartilage thickness on MRI is a structural biomarker of osteoarthritis (OA), yet anatomical variation and aging can mask early disease, including changes occurring 12-36 months before incident OA. We propose longitudinal local centile maps that use normative growth charts as prior information and integrate a knee's earlier scans to identify cartilage that is thinner or thicker than expected. We built the reference charts from 5,045 scans of 957 persistently radiographically normal knees in the Osteoarthritis Initiative. Under participant-separated nested cross-validation, longitudinal centile profiles achieved higher 12- and 24-month AUCs for predicting incident radiographic OA than regional PCA, radiomics, cross-sectional centile features, and raw-map deep features across most classifiers. These conventional descriptors added little when combined with centile profiles, and cross-sectional centiles added little beyond longitudinal centiles. Deep centile features achieved the best AUCs (0.954 [95% CI 0.931-0.974] at 12 months and 0.969 [0.949-0.985] at 24 months; balanced accuracy 0.917 and 0.931) and outperformed raw-map deep features in all 12 classifiers after correction for multiple comparisons. No representation consistently improved 36-month prediction. Longitudinal centiles transform cartilage thickness maps into reference-based deviation maps: deep longitudinal centile features provide the highest predictive accuracy, while regional longitudinal centile profiles provide interpretable prognosis with the second-highest accuracy.

papers.title: Engineering developmental transitions during human neurulation through modular integration of multimodal spatial cues
papers.abstract: Reconstituting organ development in vitro requires reproducing dynamic developmental transitions rather than only terminal tissue structures. Here, we developed MoSAIC (Modular Spatial Assembly and Integration of Cues), a modular platform that decomposes complex culture operations and subsequently integrates them to reconstruct multimodal mechano-chemical spatial cues. Using human induced pluripotent stem cells, MoSAIC enabled independent control of tissue geometry, extracellular matrix localization, physical boundaries, and morphogen gradients, while also permitting defined mechanical and chemical perturbations during development. Their integration guided a continuous ectodermal sheet through neural induction, tissue bending, and bifurcation into neural and epidermal tissues, followed by formation of a polarized neural tube structure. Spatially controlled morphogen exposure further established dorsoventral patterning, while the resulting tissue exhibited posterior neural tube identity. Using the developed model recapitulating the transition of human neurulation, MoSAIC further enables non-genetic perturbation of mechanical and chemical cues to interrogate the mechanisms governing neural tube closure.

papers.title: Structure-Guided Discovery of High-Affinity Methotrexate Aptamers for Electrochemical Drug Monitoring
papers.abstract: Methotrexate (MTX) is a narrow-therapeutic-index drug widely used in cancer and autoimmune disease treatment, for which delayed clearance can cause severe toxicity and requires close therapeutic drug monitoring. Here, we integrate high-stringency Capture-SELEX, biophysical characterization, molecular modeling, mutational validation, and electrochemical transduction to develop two structurally distinct MTX-binding DNA aptamer families. Full-length 3315 and 930 bound MTX with apparent KD values of 89 and 408 nM, respectively. Systematic truncation generated compact functional variants: 3315-55 retained 63 nM affinity and broad buffer tolerance, whereas 930-65 reached an apparent KD of 44 nM in 10 mM Mg2, revealing markedly different ion dependencies. Biolayer interferometry confirmed rapid and reversible MTX recognition, while 3315 variants retained binding in serum-containing buffer. Computational analysis and site-directed mutagenesis identified distinct recognition architectures: a compact G-rich scaffold coupled to a central binding interface in 3315 and a localized Mg2+-stabilized binding pocket in 930. Methylene blue-labeled 3315-55 and 930-65 were integrated into electrochemical aptamer-based sensors, producing concentration-dependent responses to 100-1000 uM MTX in PBS, discriminating MTX from folic acid, and responding to MTX directly in undiluted human blood. Together, these results establish a structure-guided workflow linking aptamer discovery, mechanistic validation, and electrochemical translation, providing new molecular recognition elements and a foundation for future reagent-less MTX therapeutic drug monitoring.

papers.title: Biomimetic scaffolds mimic human subretinal debris for preclinical testing of prosthetic vision
papers.abstract: Photovoltaic subretinal prostheses replace the lost photoreceptors in patients blinded by atrophic age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and provide central vision by electrically stimulating the inner retinal neurons. Subretinal debris in geographic atrophy separate the inner nuclear layer from the implant by tens of micrometers, increasing the stimulation threshold and reducing the pattern contrast. Absence of this separating layer in animal models diminishes the accuracy of preclinical testing of the next-generation implants, especially with smaller pixels. We developed three-dimensional biomimetic scaffolds nanoprinted onto photovoltaic arrays to provide a precisely controlled separation between the implants and target neurons in animal models of retinal degeneration. Gap sizes of the scaffolds were adjusted to meet the following requirements: they should allow light penetration to the implant, provide unobstructed flow of electric current, but preclude migration of cells into their 3-D structure. Gaps of 3 m were found to be optimal as they restricted cellular migration and maintained the inner nuclear layer above both planar and pillar electrode arrays. Scaffolds did not measurably alter the photovoltaic response and accurately reproduced the distance dependence of stimulation threshold. Following implantation, the initially fluid-filled intra-scaffold space was progressively filled by cellular matter matching the density of the subretinal debris. This transition is expected to increase resistivity of the scaffold to that of tissue, which was evidenced by concurrently improved grating acuity. These results establish a model of the controlled separation between the implant and the target neurons reproducing the features of subretinal debris in geographic atrophy of human patients, thereby providing a platform for accurate preclinical evaluation of the subretinal implants.

papers.title: Diffusion-Based Inference for Heterogeneous Multichannel Fluorescence Imaging
papers.abstract: Fluorescence microscopy is a central tool in biomedical image analysis, but its practical use is often constrained by incomplete and heterogeneous data. This is especially true in rare disease research, where patient cohorts are small, biological material is limited, and complex study designs frequently yield images with missing, degraded, or low-quality channels. We introduce Reliability-Mask-Conditioned DDPM (RM-DDPM), a conditional diffusion model that formulates multichannel image generation, missing-channel imputation, and degraded-channel restoration as a single reliability-guided inference problem. The model is trained on a curated subset of complete, high-quality multichannel images using a self-supervised masking objective to learn rich cross-channel dependencies from the available channels. At inference time, reliable observations condition the reverse diffusion process, allowing the same trained model to solve multiple reconstruction tasks without task-specific retraining. We evaluate RM-DDPM against task-specific baselines on one public and two in-house fluorescence microscopy datasets, comprising a rare-disease preclinical model study and a clinical patient cohort. Across these settings, RM-DDPM matches the specialized baselines in reconstruction quality, hallucinates fewer false structures, and remains more robust as degradation severity increases, while repeated sampling provides per-pixel uncertainty maps that flag unreliable reconstructions.

papers.title: Oxidative Stress and Tissue Remodeling in a Rat Abdominal Seroma Model
papers.abstract: Seroma is a common complication following abdominoplasty and other procedures involving extensive soft tissue dissection. Although animal seroma models have been reported, the stromal pathology underlying post-abdominoplasty seroma, particularly the role of oxidative stress, remains poorly characterized. Here, we developed a rat abdominal seroma model by surgically separating the subcutaneous tissue from the underlying muscle fascia and investigated the temporal evolution of the associated stromal response. Seroma developed in 9 of 20 operated rats, corresponding to a formation rate of 45.0%. Longitudinal ultrasound demonstrated that fluid accumulation peaked around postoperative day (POD) 7 and largely resolved by POD30. Despite macroscopic fluid resolution, substantial stromal remodeling persisted. Compared with normal abdominal tissue, seroma-associated tissues at POD14 and POD35 exhibited increased collagen deposition, macrophage accumulation, oxidative injury, and vascular remodeling. Additionally, at POD35, macrophage accumulation and 4-hydroxynonenal staining were greater than at POD14, whereas collagen deposition and vascular density remained elevated with no significant differences between postoperative time points. To our knowledge, this study presents the first rat model specifically designed to reproduce post-abdominoplasty seroma and the first temporal characterization of oxidative stress within seroma-associated tissue. These findings reveal that seroma fluid resolution does not coincide with stromal recovery and identify persistent oxidative stress, inflammation, fibrosis, and vascular remodeling as important features of seroma pathology.

papers.title: REZCUE: Rescuing 3D spatial omics from archived FFPE tissue
papers.abstract: Archived formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue represents a vast clinical resource, yet three-dimensional imaging and molecular profiling remain largely incompatible because current antigen retrieval and clearing can degrade nucleic acids. We developed REZCUE, a depth-invariant antigen retrieval chemistry based on in situ protein refolding that enables 3D multiplexed immunofluorescence imaging of intact FFPE tissue while preserving DNA, RNA, and protein for subsequent assays. REZCUE restores antigenicity in tissue archived for up to 30 years, supports 160 commercial antibodies across tissue types, and enables imaging to 4 mm depth. Imaging before destructive molecular profiling establishes a 3D spatial reference for registering molecular assays to intact tissue architecture. In a 25-year-archived breast cancer specimen, REZCUE integrated 3D image-guided clonal segmentation with spatial transcriptomics, mass spectrometry, miRNA sequencing, and whole-genome sequencing, identifying a luminalB/HER2-positive clone missed by conventional section-based spatial-omics. REZCUE transforms archived FFPE specimens into spatially registered substrates for sequential 3D multi-omic interrogation.

papers.title: Cutting-edge microfluidic technology allows detection and sorting of single fluorescent extracellular vesicles
papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EV) are cell-secreted, nanosized biological particles that are involved in most physiological and pathophysiological processes. Their composition and properties reflect the pathophysiological state of the producing cell, tissue, and organ. Released into biological fluids, they may be used as a potential source of non-invasive biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis or therapeutic follow-up in several diseases such as cancer. However, despite the development of single-EV analysis technologies, the sorting of EV subpopulations for downstream analysis remains a major challenge. Here, we describe a novel instrument that combines a highly sensitive optical detection system with an advanced lab-on-a-chip device. Using engineered fluorescent small extracellular vesicles (sEV), we demonstrate that the Hekat NanoSorter enables sensitive, scalable, and reproducible detection and sorting of individual sEVs for downstream analysis by cryo-EM. Furthermore, detailed characterization of the sorted EV populations, together with the detection of sEVs labeled with an in vitro pathophysiological marker, demonstrates the ability of the NanoSorter to monitor and enrich clinically relevant EV-associated biomarkers. These findings highlight the clinical potential of extracellular vesicle sorting for their use as biomarkers for therapeutic monitoring and treatment outcome assessment.

papers.title: Generalizing Protein Fitness Prediction Across Distribution Shifts via Structural and Co-evolutionary Priors
papers.abstract: Protein fitness prediction is essential for protein engineering. Recent fitness-landscape benchmarks such as FLIP2 have shown that methods performing well under conventional train-test splits can fail when the test set is shifted out of distribution (OOD), including mutations at unseen positions and variants from unseen protein backbones. In particular, current protein language models (pLMs) often suffer substantial performance degradation under such distribution shifts, limiting their practical use in protein engineering. We therefore develop a framework that augments sequence representations with structural and co-evolutionary information for fitness prediction. Specifically, we pair structure-aware pLMs with features pooled from an AlphaFold-style trunk applied to each sequence and its multiple sequence alignment (MSA), and use a lightweight prediction probe to map these frozen representations to fitness scores. Our framework consistently outperforms the best previously reported FLIP2 scores across several types of distribution shift. We then systematically study the contribution of each component in our framework to generalization. Structural priors yield the largest performance gains on held-out protein backbones, whereas trunk features improve generalization to held-out mutation positions. Rather than proposing a single best method, we characterize which modalities are effective for different protein families and distribution shifts, providing practical guidance for choosing representations according to the generalization regime. These findings support the development of more generalizable fitness predictors that can serve as effective reward functions or oracles for protein design toward desired functions.

papers.title: Oxygen-permeable microwell plates for high-throughput spheroid culture
papers.abstract: Oxygen (O2) transport is a major limitation in high-density cell culture, particularly as three-dimensional (3D) spheroids are increasingly used to better mimic in vivo tissue environments. Here, we developed a poly(4-methyl-1-pentene) (PMP)-based microwell platform, leveraging its lower molecular absorption and greater mechanical stability than the commonly used O2-permeable polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), while retaining high O2 permeability. We measured O2 permeability in 50-m-thick PMP membranes and found approximately 200-fold greater O2 permeability than the conventional 1-mm polystyrene culture-plate material. PMP membrane-based microwell plates with 350-m-diameter wells maintained spatial separation of pre-formed hepatocyte spheroids while supplying O2 from the plate bottom, synergistically enhancing spheroid oxygenation. Compared with non-O2-permeable plates, the platform reduced localized hypoxia and hypoxia-associated cell injury while improving spheroid viability and growth. Collectively, PMP-based O2-permeable microwell plates provide a promising, scalable, high-throughput platform for spheroid culture with multiple applications in tissue engineering, drug screening and beyond.

papers.title: Pulsed Field Ablation Enables Stromal Manipulation and Tumor Reduction in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by a dense desmoplastic microenvironment that promotes therapeutic resistance and disease progression. Here, we investigated the impact of pulsed field ablation (PFA), a non-thermal electroporation-based therapy, on tumor and stromal remodeling in a syngeneic murine PDAC model. PFA induced rapid apoptotic and necrotic tumor cell death, transient neutrophil infiltration, and durable suppression of tumor growth. Single-cell RNA sequencing following repeated PFA treatments revealed enrichment of a classical secretory tumor cell state associated with complement and stress-response pathways and reduced epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) programs. Although overall immune composition was largely unchanged, PFA markedly remodeled the stromal compartment, decreasing SMA-positive activation and shifting cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) from tumor-promoting myofibroblastic CAFs toward Dpp4+ complement-secreting CAFs. This transition was accompanied by increased IL-1 signaling potential, reduced Tgfb1 expression, and diminished tumor cell TGF-{beta} response signatures. Serial PFA treatments further suppressed EMT-associated programs, identifying stromal reprogramming as a potential mechanism through which PFA enhances tumor control.
